findings.title: Hung spawn workers are not killed before their replacements start
findings.body: Workers are created with `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which produces a `SpawnProcess` that is not an instance of the top-level `multiprocessing.Process` class. Consequently this guard is false in production. When a worker is declared hung, it is left running and a replacement is started for the same shards. If the original worker recovers, both workers can flush and produce the same Redis segments concurrently, causing duplicate buffered-segment messages and conflicting backpressure/health updates. Check against the spawn context's base process type (or capability) and join/kill the old worker before replacing it.

findings.title: The default CLI configuration still creates only one flusher worker
findings.body: Click always supplies the default `flusher_processes=1` to `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory`, so `SpanFlusher` receives a limit of one rather than its per-shard fallback. Thus a normal `process-spans` invocation without an explicit flag continues to run a single flusher even when it owns multiple Redis shards, and the stated per-shard parallelization/capacity improvement is never enabled by default. Use a per-shard default (for example, pass `None` through to `SpanFlusher`) or configure the intended shard-count limit in the consumer's default deployment arguments.

findings.title: `--flusher-processes` accepts invalid values that can prevent consumer startup
findings.body: The option accepts any integer. A negative value is truthy in `SpanFlusher`, making `num_processes` negative; no process-map entries are created and assigning the first shard then raises a `KeyError`. A value of zero is silently treated as false and instead creates one worker per assigned shard, violating the requested maximum. Restrict the option to integers of at least one (and validate the constructor as well for non-CLI callers).

findings.title: The added wait is disabled by the test's own sleep monkeypatch
findings.body: This test replaces `time.sleep` with a no-op at line 15, so `time.sleep(0.1)` does not give the flusher thread time to observe the changed drift. `step.join()` can therefore set the stop flag before the thread flushes, making the assertion dependent on thread scheduling and allowing intermittent tuple-unpacking failures or false coverage. Preserve the real sleep for this synchronization point or use an event/polling condition that waits for `messages`.
